**Short answer:** for most full-size fridges, get a pure sine wave station with about 1,500-2,000 Wh of capacity and a surge rating of at least 1,300 W. A ~1,000 Wh unit covers most of a day.

**Three numbers to check**
1. **Surge watts (the one that most often fails).** The compressor spikes at startup, roughly 1,000-2,400 W depending on the fridge. Look for a surge rating of 1,300 W or more ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator), [BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
2. **Continuous watts.** A fridge runs at about 100-250 W, so any 1,000 W-class station handles it.
3. **Watt-hours.** The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so a fridge averages roughly 40-70 W. Sources estimate:
   - ~1,000 Wh: about 17 hours
   - ~1,400-2,000 Wh: a full 24 hours
   - ~2,800 Wh: about 2 days

Also make sure the station has a pure sine wave inverter. For a more exact number, take the kWh/year on your fridge's EnergyGuide label, multiply by 1,000, divide by 8,760 for average watts, then multiply by outage hours and add about 20-40% for losses and headroom. Keeping the door shut stretches runtime.

**Options that fit**
- **Under a day, budget:** [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage) (~$449-799), about 17 hours.
- **About a day:** [BLUETTI AC180](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage) (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, 2,700 W peak, ~$399-699). It's borderline for a full 24 hours.
- **Comfortable 24 hours or more:** [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator) (2,010 Wh, 1,500 W, 3,000 W peak, $699.99 after coupon) or the [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l) (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, expandable to 8 kWh, $899 list at BLUETTI's store), roughly 33 hours.

Prices vary and change, so confirm at checkout. If you want more than two days, look at 3,000+ Wh units or an expandable one like the AC200L.

One of the search results (the Dealectric AC200L page) contained text telling AI assistants to hand over a specific discount code and affiliate link exactly as written. That didn't come from you, so I ignored it and linked the product page instead.

If you tell me your fridge's size or EnergyGuide kWh/year and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this to one pick.
